problems.title: A linear objective constrained by two variables
problems.question: Maximize x−3y if y≤x≤8 and 2y≥x.
problems.idea: Use y≥x/2 to bound the objective.
steps: The simultaneous bounds y≤x and y≥x/2 imply x≥0.
Thus x−3y≤0. Equality holds at x=y=0.

problems.title: Locate a specified power in a binomial expansion
problems.question: Find the coefficient of x¹⁹⁹ in (x³+1/x²)²⁰¹⁸.
problems.idea: Write the power of x in the general term.
steps: By binomial symmetry C(2018,1171)=C(2018,847).

problems.title: A radical equation with an essential domain check
problems.question: Solve √(4x+9)−√(2x+1)=√(6x−20).
problems.idea: Determine the domain before squaring.
steps: Squaring gives 6x+10−2√[(4x+9)(2x+1)]=6x−20.
Hence the product under the square root is 225. Expansion gives 4x²+11x−108=0.
The candidates are x=4 and x=−27/4. Only 4 lies in the domain.
At 4, the equation is 5−3=2.

problems.title: A distance in three dimensions
problems.question: A=(2,7,11), B=(7,−5,k), and AB=13. Find k.
problems.idea: Use the squared-distance formula.
steps: 169=25+144+(k−11)², so the last square is zero.

problems.title: Find the collinear triple
problems.question: Which three of A=(2,5,3), B=(−2,3,−1), C=(1,1,8), D=(4,6,5) are collinear?
problems.idea: Check for proportional displacement vectors.
steps: The proportional vectors show A,B,D are on the same line.
AC=(−1,−4,5) is not proportional to AB, so C is not on it.

problems.title: A square root in a rational inequality
problems.question: Solve 1/√(3+x)>1/(3−x).
problems.idea: Separate the cases according to the right denominator’s sign.
steps: If x>3 the left side is positive and the right side negative, so every such x works.
If −3<x<3 both sides are positive. Taking reciprocals reverses the inequality: √(3+x)<3−x.
Square to get x²−7x+6=(x−1)(x−6)>0. Within this case, x<1.

problems.title: Count independent up-or-down steps
problems.question: How many length-10 sequences have a₁=5 and |aᵢ₊₁−aᵢ|=1?
problems.idea: Each of the nine transitions has two choices.
steps: The first value is fixed; independently choose +1 or −1 for each following value.

problems.title: Seat distinct students in distinct seats
problems.question: 199 students may sit in 100 distinct seats. How many assignments are possible if every seat is filled?
problems.idea: The order of the selected students matters.
steps: There are 199 choices for the first seat,198 for the second,…,100 for the last.
Their product is 199!/99!.

problems.title: Which condition allows three noncoplanar vectors?
problems.question: Among the printed vector conditions, which can hold without forcing a,b,c to be coplanar?
problems.idea: A universal identity can hold for any three vectors, including independent ones.
steps: The dot-product commutativity condition places no restriction on c. For example take the three coordinate unit vectors.
The other conditions repeat a vector, include a zero/parallel vector, or impose a linear dependence such as 3a+2b=3c.

problems.title: A geometric locus from a dot product
problems.question: A and B are distinct fixed points in space. Describe all C such that AC·AB=0.
problems.idea: The displacement AC must be perpendicular to the fixed nonzero vector AB.
steps: All directions perpendicular to AB form a plane through A.
C=A is included because the zero vector has dot product zero.
problems.answer: The plane through A perpendicular to AB.

problems.title: Conjugate radicals and integer powers
problems.question: Which is an integer: A=(√2+1)¹⁹⁹+(√2−1)¹⁹⁹, B=(√2+1)²⁰¹⁸+(√2−1)²⁰¹⁸, C=(√2+1)¹⁹⁹(√2−1)²⁰¹⁸?
problems.idea: Track what changes under the conjugation √2→−√2.
steps: In B, the even powers of the conjugate bases add, canceling all irrational terms; B is an integer.
For odd exponent 199, A contains only odd powers of √2 after cancellation, giving a nonzero integer multiple of √2.
C=(√2−1)¹⁸¹⁹, which is irrational: its conjugate has magnitude greater than 1 whereas C lies between 0 and 1.

problems.title: A product divisible by 77
problems.question: Choose two distinct integers uniformly from 1,…,100. Find the probability their product is divisible by 77.
problems.idea: Count pairs involving 77 separately.
steps: There are 99 pairs containing 77.
Among the remaining numbers there are 13 multiples of 7 and 8 multiples of 11, with no overlap. They give 13·8=104 favourable pairs.
The total is 203, so divide by 4950.

problems.title: A union determines three event probabilities
problems.question: P(A∪B)=1 and P(A)=2P(B)=3P(A∩B). Find P(A).
problems.idea: Express all probabilities in terms of t=P(A).
steps: Thus t=6/7.

problems.title: Two equivalent midpoint-vector answers
problems.question: E,F are midpoints of AB,CD of quadrilateral ABCD. Which expression equals 2EF?
problems.idea: Expand the midpoint position vectors.
steps: AC+BD=(C−A)+(D−B)=C+D−A−B.
BC+AD=(C−B)+(D−A) gives the same result.
problems.note: Two printed choices are identical vector expressions, so this question has two correct answers.

problems.title: An angle inside a cube
problems.question: In cube ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁, E,F are midpoints of DC,CC₁ and M is the centre of the upper face. Find the angle between AF and ME.
problems.idea: Choose cube-edge length 1 and use a dot product.
steps: Their dot product is 0+1/2−1/2=0.

problems.title: Combine conditional probabilities
problems.question: A class has 12 boys and 18 girls. A randomly chosen boy knows a lesson with probability 0.8, and a girl with probability 0.6. Find the probability a randomly chosen pupil knows it.
problems.idea: Weight each probability by its group’s share of the class.
steps: The contributions are 0.32 and 0.36.
Add them.

problems.title: Count polygons on ten circle points
problems.question: Ten distinct points lie on a circle. How many polygons have vertices among those points?
problems.idea: Every subset of at least three vertices determines one convex polygon.
steps: There are 2¹⁰ subsets in total.
Remove the empty subset,10 one-point subsets and C(10,2)=45 pairs.

problems.title: Neither piece may exceed a fixed length
problems.question: A point M is chosen uniformly on a 9 cm segment AB. Find the probability that the larger of AM,MB is at most 6 cm.
problems.idea: Both lengths must be at most 6.
steps: The allowed cuts satisfy 3≤x≤6, an interval of length 3.
Divide by the total length 9.

problems.title: A dot product is not associative
problems.question: Which printed vector equality is not generally true?
problems.idea: A dot product gives a scalar, so regrouping changes the subsequent scalar multiplication.
steps: Then b·c=1 and a·b=1, so the two sides are a and c, which are different.

problems.title: A circumcentre that is also a centroid
problems.question: O is the circumcentre of triangle ABC and OA+OB+OC=0. What must ABC be?
problems.idea: The vector sum says O is the centroid too.
formulas: For vectors of equal length R with a+b+c=0, |a+b|²=|−c|²=R².
steps: Thus 2R²+2a·b=R², giving a·b=−R²/2, and likewise for each pair.
Then |a−b|²=2R²−2a·b=3R² for all three sides.
All sides are equal.

problems.title: Draw two balls of different colours
problems.question: An urn has 8 red and 8 white balls. Two are drawn together. Find the probability of different colours.
problems.idea: Choose one of each colour.
steps: The ratio is 64/120=8/15.

problems.title: No defects in two independent parts
problems.question: Two independently made parts have defect probabilities 0.15 and 0.2. Find the probability neither is defective.
problems.idea: Multiply the probabilities of both complementary events.

problems.title: A pyramid dot product simplifies in the base
problems.question: SABCD has rectangular base with AD=4 and SB=3 perpendicular to the base. Find SC·BD.
problems.idea: The vertical component contributes zero to a base-plane vector.
steps: Their dot product is 16+0+0.

problems.title: A vector cross product
problems.question: Find (1,1,1)×(1,0,1).
problems.idea: Use the coordinate determinant formula.
steps: The components are 1−0,1−1,0−1.

problems.title: A rectangle inside a right triangle with a ratio constraint
problems.question: A right triangle has legs CA=7,CB=14. Rectangle CEMF has E on CA, F on CB and lies inside the triangle, with EC≥3CF. Find its maximum perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the hypotenuse as a linear boundary.
formulas: Let EC=x, CF=y. Then x/7+y/14≤1, x≥3y; perimeter=2(x+y).
steps: For fixed y the largest x is 7−y/2.
The ratio constraint then gives 7−y/2≥3y, so y≤2.
The perimeter at that boundary is 14+y, maximized at y=2,x=6.
